acceptance: SQL and DataFrame power, throughput and maintenance tests stop at the deadline, shown by tests.
No BenchBox-imposed stream or query limit remains; a user-set one still works.
The timing table against the commit before step 1a is recorded, within 2% or approved by the owner.
description:
## Problem
After step 1 the deadline is checked between phases and in the generic SQL query loop only. Not yet covered: power, throughput and maintenance tests (platforms/base/execution.py `_execute_*_test`, core/throughput/runner.py, the TPC-H and TPC-DS test classes) and the DataFrame executor (platforms/dataframe/benchmark_mixin.py:319, loop near :1279; dataframe/tpch_full_spec.py:128). BenchBox also enforces stream limits of its own: `TPCDSThroughputTestConfig.stream_timeout = 7200` (core/tpcds/throughput_test.py:38) and TPC-H 3600 (core/tpch/throughput_test.py:52), applied through execution.py. Unenforced or dead: TPC-DS and TPC-H `query_timeout` 300 (the TPC-DS runner says it "no longer has any effect"); an after-the-fact check at core/tpcds/benchmark/runner.py:1017 whose only caller passes no value; `experimental/load_testing/executor.py:73,373` (300 s default with an after-the-fact check).

## Owner decisions
Execution defaults: "remove them, in line with 'no default timeout'. The settings stay available for a user to set; they just have no value unless set. The after-the-fact check is deleted." Timing: "if the medians differ by more than 2%, I stop and bring you the numbers before arming. Otherwise I put the table in the pull request and continue." ('I' is the agent.) Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
1. Power, throughput and maintenance tests, SQL and DataFrame, check the deadline between queries, streams and operations. The effective stream limit is the smaller of the user's stream setting and the time remaining.
2. When the deadline passes, running streams are signalled to stop whatever `cancel_on_timeout` is: the deadline creates and sets the stream events itself (today they exist only when `cancel_on_timeout` is set, core/throughput/runner.py:106-116).
3. GizmoSQL's per-query cancel (`adbc_cancel`, gizmosql.py:252-271) receives the time remaining. Onehouse has `cancel_job` but nothing calls it; leave it for step 3.
4. Remove the enforced stream defaults (7200 and 3600): unset means no limit, represented by the existing 0 sentinel that execution.py:121,137 already treats as disabled, so readers that compare with `> 0` or `< 1` keep working (core/throughput/runner.py:95, core/tpcds/benchmark/runner.py:817-820). Delete the dead `query_timeout` parameters' defaults and the after-the-fact checks (tpcds runner :1017 and the load-testing executor's), listing every reader in the pull request.
5. Queries not run because of the deadline are absent from the result; a query in flight when the run stops is recorded with status TIMEOUT.
6. Changelog and docs: streams no longer stop at 3600 or 7200 seconds unless the user sets a limit.

## Decision gates
A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). The 0 sentinel is the repository's existing convention and the owner chose 0 = no limit. If a test tier or UAT config relied on a removed default, set the old value explicitly in that configuration and list each place in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop). Timing proof: TPC-H SF 1 on DuckDB, power phase, five runs on the commit before step 1a and five on this branch, one at a time through `make heavy-run`, same machine; compare the median of total query time. More than 2% apart: stop, do not arm, bring the table. No change to how results are computed.

## Verification rubric
Pass, each by a test that fails before the change:
- SQL power, throughput and maintenance tests each stop at the deadline with a stubbed slow query or operation; the in-flight query is TIMEOUT and later ones are absent.
- A DataFrame power run and a DataFrame throughput run stop at the deadline (for example polars-df with a stubbed slow query).
- With the default config (`cancel_on_timeout` false) the stream events are set when the deadline passes.
- The effective stream limit is min(user setting, remaining).
- Through the adapter path, with nothing set, a stubbed TPC-H stream that outlives 3600 s and a TPC-DS stream that outlives 7200 s are not stopped; a user-set stream limit still stops one.
- The after-the-fact checks are gone (assert the code path, not merely 'not stopped').
- GizmoSQL receives the remaining time.
- A deadline check does not sit between the start and stop of a query timer in any touched loop.
The ten-run timing table with heavy-run log paths is in the pull request, or the item is blocked with the table. `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents implement batch members and serial items under the delivery plan on run-timeout-plan-20261120 (owner, 2026-11-21); a batch member makes no tracker write, opens no pull request and stops at a landing report. A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
